cards.name: Cineon Converter
cards.summary: Old version of Cineon Converter: converts 10-bit logarithmic Cineon/DPX film-scan footage to linear (or linear to log) using film black/white points, gamma and a highlight roll-off. On normal footage it shifts contrast and brightness heavily.
use_for: Normalising archival Cineon/DPX film scans in a documentary so they show normal contrast
Viewing a flat Cineon-log telecine/DPX transfer normally before grading
Deliberately flattening a shot to a washed-out log look (Linear to Log) for a 'raw footage' reveal
avoid: Applying to ordinary Rec.709 camera or press footage: it crushes or blows out the image
Camera log footage (S-Log, V-Log, C-Log, LogC): Cineon is a different curve, use the camera's LUT (Apply Color LUT / Lumetri) instead
Using this legacy match name in new builds: use 'ADBE Cineon Converter2' instead

params.name: Conversion Type
params.does: Direction of the conversion (log to linear, linear to log, log to log)
params.typical: keep default 3 (renders as Log to Linear on normal footage: contrast expands)

params.name: 10 Bit Black Point
params.does: Code value treated as black in the 10-bit log source

params.name: 10 Bit White Point
params.does: Code value treated as white in the 10-bit log source

params.name: Internal Black Point
params.does: Where log black lands in the output (normalised 0-1)

params.name: Internal White Point
params.does: Where log white lands in the output (normalised 0-1)

params.name: Gamma
params.does: Film gamma used for the conversion

params.name: Highlight Rolloff
params.does: Softens how highlights clip to white

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Cineon Converter (ADBE Cineon Converter2, Utility); Premiere: Cineon Converter (Utility), which runs this same legacy engine (AE.ADBE Cineon Converter) with a 0-based Conversion Type (0 Linear to Log, 1 Log to Linear, 2 Log to Log)
cards.scripting: Obsolete: apply 'ADBE Cineon Converter2' instead; it has the same property names (its Conversion Type is a clean 1-3 popup: 1 Linear to Log, 2 Log to Linear, 3 Log to Log). Here Conversion Type is a 1-6 popup (read from After Effects 26.0): 1 Log to Linear (obsolete), 2 Linear to Log, 3 Log to Linear (the default), 4 Log to Log, 5 Log to Linear (obsolete), 6 Log to Log (obsolete); a test render with default 3 on normal footage expanded contrast (highlights clip, shadows crush), the Log to Linear behaviour. Internal Black/White Point are normalised 0-1, the 10 Bit points are raw code values 0-1023.

verified.note: With all defaults (Conversion Type 3) the frame gets much harsher contrast: background highlights blow to white and dark clothing crushes, the heavy contrast/brightness shift the summary predicts and consistent with Log to Linear.

cards.name: Color Balance
cards.summary: Old three-slider Color Balance: shifts the whole image toward or away from red, green and blue (-100 to 100 each) to add or remove a global colour cast. It has no shadow/midtone/highlight split.
use_for: Neutralising a colour cast on archival or phone footage in a documentary
Quick warm (red up, blue down) or cool (blue up) cast on a flashback or B-roll
Matching two press clips that came from different cameras
avoid: Large values: a channel clips and skin goes garish
Using it for grading where shadows and highlights need different tints: use Color Balance (ADBE Color Balance 2) or Lumetri Color

params.name: Red Balance
params.does: Adds red (positive) or cyan (negative) across the image

params.name: Green Balance
params.does: Adds green (positive) or magenta (negative)

params.name: Blue Balance
params.does: Adds blue (positive) or yellow (negative)

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Color Balance (ADBE Color Balance 2, Color Correction); Premiere: Color Balance (RGB) or Lumetri Color
cards.scripting: Obsolete: apply 'ADBE Color Balance 2' (9 sliders: Shadow/Midtone/Highlight x Red/Green/Blue Balance, -100..100) instead. Exact per-unit behaviour of this legacy version is not verified; 0 on all three is neutral.

verified.note: Red +30 / Blue -30 gives a strong orange-amber cast over the whole frame (shadows go brown, whites go cream), a clear global colour shift.

cards.name: Exposure
cards.summary: Old version of Exposure: brightens or darkens the image in photographic stops, with Offset (lifts/crushes blacks) and Gamma, either for the master or per RGB channel, computed in linear light.
use_for: Rescuing a dark interview or night press shot by +0.5 to +1.5 stops
Flash-to-white or camera-flash hit between two news shots (animate Exposure up and back)
Darkening a background plate behind lower-thirds or titles
avoid: Values beyond about +/-5 stops give a solid white or black frame
Using this legacy match name: apply 'ADBE Exposure2' instead

params.name: Channels:
params.does: Master (one control) or Individual Channels (per-RGB controls)

params.name: Exposure
params.does: Master brightness change in stops

params.name: Offset
params.does: Adds/subtracts a constant: lifts or crushes blacks

params.name: Gamma
params.does: Midtone gamma (1 = unchanged)

params.name: Red Exposure
params.does: Red channel exposure, only with Channels: = 2

params.name: Blue Exposure
params.does: Blue channel exposure, only with Channels: = 2

params.name: Bypass Linear Light Conversion
params.does: Checkbox: apply the adjustment to the raw (gamma-encoded) pixel values instead of converting to linear light first; changes how the stops scale in a normal non-linear project

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Exposure (ADBE Exposure2, Color Correction); Premiere: Lumetri Color (Basic Correction > Exposure)
cards.scripting: Obsolete: apply 'ADBE Exposure2' instead. Note the rename: this legacy version calls the gamma controls 'Gamma' / 'Red Gamma' / 'Green Gamma' / 'Blue Gamma', while Exposure2 uses 'Gamma Correction' (check names in its card). Per-channel properties only act when 'Channels:' = 2; set it first. Bypass Linear Light Conversion is a 0/1 checkbox.

verified.note: +1.5 stops brightens the whole frame strongly: the white wall and white stripes clip toward white and the dark clothing lifts to grey-blue, a clear overexposed look.

cards.name: Fast Blur (Legacy)
cards.summary: Legacy fast blur: an approximated Gaussian-style blur of the whole layer, horizontal, vertical or both. Superseded by the GPU Gaussian Blur and Fast Box Blur.
use_for: Blurring a background plate behind titles or a quote card
Blur-in / blur-out transitions between news shots
Hiding unusable detail (logos, faces of bystanders) on B-roll: it blurs the whole layer, so put it on a masked duplicate layer
avoid: Leaving Repeat Edge Pixels at 0 on full-frame footage: edges go dark/transparent
Using this legacy match name in new builds: use 'ADBE Gaussian Blur 2' or 'ADBE Box Blur2'

params.name: Blurriness
params.does: Blur amount in pixels

params.name: Blur Dimensions
params.does: Blur both directions, horizontal only or vertical only
params.typical: 1 (Horizontal and Vertical); 2 for a horizontal smear

params.name: Repeat Edge Pixels
params.does: Checkbox: extend edge pixels so frame edges stay solid

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Gaussian Blur (ADBE Gaussian Blur 2) or Fast Box Blur (ADBE Box Blur2); Premiere: Fast Blur (AE.ADBE Fast Blur, this same engine, dropdown 0-based) or Gaussian Blur (Legacy) for the same Blurriness-style controls (Premiere's new 'Gaussian Blur' uses different property names)
cards.scripting: Obsolete: apply 'ADBE Gaussian Blur 2' (Blurriness, Blur Dimensions, Repeat Edge Pixels: same names) instead. Blur Dimensions is a 1-based popup; Repeat Edge Pixels is 0/1. Blurriness range runs to 30000 but values above a few hundred are pointless.

verified.note: Blurriness 40 in both directions turns the frame into a heavy soft defocus where faces and small motifs are unreadable, edges stay solid.

cards.name: Levels
cards.summary: Old version of Levels: remaps input black/white points, midtone gamma and output black/white to set contrast and brightness. Values are normalised 0-1.
use_for: Adding contrast to flat news or archival footage
Faded / lifted-black look for documentary flashbacks (raise Output Black)
Darkening a shot under lower-thirds
avoid: Pulling Input Black/White too far: clipped skin tones and posterised skies
Using this legacy match name: apply 'ADBE Easy Levels2' instead

params.name: Channel:
params.does: Which channel the UI histogram and sliders edit (RGB, Red, Green, Blue, Alpha)

params.name: Input Black
params.does: Input level mapped to black (0-1)

params.name: Input White
params.does: Input level mapped to white (0-1)

params.name: Gamma
params.does: Midtone brightness (1 = unchanged, <1 darker, >1 brighter)

params.name: Output Black
params.does: Lowest output level: raise for faded blacks

params.name: Output White
params.does: Highest output level: lower to dull highlights

params.name: Clip To Output Black
params.does: Checkbox: clamp results below Output Black

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Levels (ADBE Easy Levels2, Color Correction); Premiere: Levels (different names and units: '(RGB) Black Input Level' 0-255, '(RGB) Gamma' x100) or Lumetri Color
cards.scripting: Obsolete: apply 'ADBE Easy Levels2' instead. Difference: here Clip To Output Black/White are 0/1 checkboxes; in Easy Levels2 they are 1-3 popups. Values normalised 0-1 (1.0 = 255 in 8 bpc). Only the master (RGB) sliders are harvested as properties; how they behave when 'Channel:' is set to another channel is not verified, so leave 'Channel:' at 1 and use 'Levels (Individual Controls)' (ADBE Pro Levels2) for per-channel work. 'Histogram' is a custom display property and cannot be set.

verified.note: Input Black 0.1 / Input White 0.85 / Gamma 0.9 makes the frame visibly punchier: brighter whites and deeper darks than the flat baseline.

cards.name: Levels (Individual Controls)
cards.summary: Old version of Levels (Individual Controls): the same black/white/gamma remapping as Levels but with every channel (RGB master, Red, Green, Blue, Alpha) exposed as separate properties, so it can tint and grade per channel.
use_for: Per-channel grade: warm highlights / cool shadows on documentary B-roll
Faded film look by raising Output Black on one channel (e.g. blue for blue-tinted shadows)
Tightening alpha edges of a key (Alpha Input Black/White)
avoid: Unbalanced per-channel gammas give ugly green/magenta skin
Using this legacy match name: apply 'ADBE Pro Levels2' instead

params.name: Input Black
params.does: RGB master input black (0-1)

params.name: Input White
params.does: RGB master input white (0-1)

params.name: Gamma
params.does: RGB master midtone gamma

params.name: Red Gamma
params.does: Red midtones: >1 warmer, <1 cooler

params.name: Blue Gamma
params.does: Blue midtones: >1 cooler, <1 warmer

params.name: Blue Output Black
params.does: Lifts blue in the shadows (blue-tinted, faded shadows)

params.name: Alpha Input Black
params.does: Alpha input black point: raise to cut away faint semi-transparent fringe of a matte

params.name: Alpha Input White
params.does: Alpha input white point: lower to make semi-transparent areas of the matte solid

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Levels (Individual Controls) (ADBE Pro Levels2, Color Correction); Premiere: Levels (has per-channel '(R)/(G)/(B) ...' controls, 0-255 units, gamma x100) or Lumetri Color (RGB Curves)
cards.scripting: Obsolete: apply 'ADBE Pro Levels2' instead (same per-channel property names). All values normalised 0-1. 'Channel:' only changes which histogram the UI shows. Here Clip To Output Black/White are 0/1 checkboxes (popups 1-3 in Pro Levels2).

verified.note: Visible per-channel tint: Red Gamma 1.2 plus Blue Output Black 0.15 shift the whole frame toward magenta/lavender, the navy areas turn purple and the white wall goes pinkish.

cards.name: Noise
cards.summary: Old version of Noise: adds random per-pixel noise (colour or monochrome) that changes every frame, for a grainy video-noise texture.
use_for: Light grain to blend stock or AI shots into real news footage
Gritty 'leaked footage' / CCTV texture in an explainer
Adding texture over flat graphics or backgrounds so they do not band
avoid: Amount above about 30 looks like a broken signal, not film grain
Using this legacy match name: apply 'ADBE Noise2' instead

params.name: Amount of Noise
params.does: Noise strength in percent

params.name: Noise Type
params.does: Checkbox: 1 = colour noise, 0 = monochrome

params.name: Clipping
params.does: Checkbox: clip noisy values so the image does not wash out

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Noise (ADBE Noise2, Noise & Grain); Premiere: Noise (AE.ADBE Noise2; there the checkboxes are named 'Use Color Noise' and 'Clip Result Values')
cards.scripting: Obsolete: apply 'ADBE Noise2' instead (same three property names). Noise Type (UI label 'Use Color Noise') and Clipping ('Clip Result Values') are 0/1 checkboxes. Noise re-randomises every frame automatically; no keyframes needed.

verified.note: Fine colour speckle now reads clearly over the whole frame with faces, stripes and foreground blocks intact; Amount 50 is visibly grainier than the old Amount 25 render, where the noise all but vanished after downscaling.

cards.name: Noise Alpha
cards.summary: Old version of Noise Alpha: adds random noise to the layer's alpha channel, so the layer becomes speckled or dissolves in noisy patches over whatever is underneath.
use_for: Noisy dissolve-in of a title or logo
Speckled 'broken signal' breakup of a graphic layer
Rough grunge edge on a text card
avoid: Expecting a change on a full-frame opaque layer with nothing under it: only alpha changes
Using this legacy match name: apply 'ADBE Noise Alpha2' instead

params.name: Noise
params.does: Noise style popup (Uniform/Squared Random, Uniform/Squared Animation)

params.name: Amount
params.does: How much alpha noise is added (0-100 here)

params.name: Original Alpha
params.does: How the noise combines with the existing alpha (Add, Clamp, Scale, Edges)

params.name: Overflow
params.does: How values outside 0-255 are handled (Clip, Wrap Back, Wrap)

params.name: Contextual Control
params.does: Random Seed (Random noise types) or Noise Phase (Animation types); animate to change the pattern

params.name: Cycle Noise
params.does: Checkbox: make animated noise loop

params.name: Cycle (in Revolutions)
params.does: Revolutions before the noise loop repeats

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Noise Alpha (ADBE Noise Alpha2, Noise & Grain); no Premiere equivalent in v26
cards.scripting: Obsolete: apply 'ADBE Noise Alpha2' instead (same property names, but its Amount runs 0-10000 while this one harvests 0-100). Original Alpha (1 Add, 2 Clamp, 3 Scale, 4 Edges), Overflow (1 Clip, 2 Wrap Back, 3 Wrap) and Noise (1 Uniform Random, 2 Squared Random, 3 a separator, 4 Uniform Animation, 5 Squared Animation) are read from After Effects 26.0. 'Contextual Control' is the seed/phase control whose UI label changes with the Noise type; it has no harvested range. Result shows only over another layer or a coloured comp background.

verified.note: Fine speckled transparent holes over the whole layer let the black comp background through, giving a darker, dusty, eroded texture as described.

cards.name: Noise HLS
cards.summary: Old version of Noise HLS: adds noise separately to hue, lightness and saturation, with an optional film-grain mode and grain size. The noise is static unless Noise Phase is animated.
use_for: Controlled film grain (lightness-only noise) on documentary archival recreations
Colour speckle for a damaged-tape look
Matching grain between AI-generated and real footage
avoid: Hue noise above a small amount turns skin into rainbow speckle
Using this legacy match name: apply 'ADBE Noise HLS2' instead

params.name: Noise
params.does: Noise style: Uniform, Squared or Grain

params.name: Lightness
params.does: Amount of brightness noise
params.typical: 0.1-0.5 (1 = 100%; 8 wiped the image to static in a test render)

params.name: Saturation
params.does: Amount of saturation noise

params.name: Hue
params.does: Amount of hue noise

params.name: Grain Size
params.does: Grain size, only with Noise = 3

params.name: Noise Phase
params.does: Seed/phase of the pattern; animate to make grain move

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Noise HLS (ADBE Noise HLS2, Noise & Grain); Premiere: Noise (no HLS variant in v26)
cards.scripting: Obsolete: apply 'ADBE Noise HLS2' instead. Hue/Lightness/Saturation harvest here as 0-10 (Noise HLS2 harvests 0-1000), and a test render confirmed the scale is 1 = 100% (Lightness 8 / Saturation 4 / Hue 1 turned the frame into pure static): divide Noise HLS2 values by 100 (30 there = 0.3 here). Noise popup: 1 Uniform, 2 Squared, 3 Grain. Noise Phase has no range; without keyframes the grain is frozen.

verified.note: The picture is back: an even film-grain speckle sits over the intact picture with no rainbow on faces, where the old Lightness 8 / Saturation 4 / Hue 1 render was pure grey-white static.

cards.name: Noise HLS Auto
cards.summary: Old version of Noise HLS Auto: the same hue/lightness/saturation noise as Noise HLS, but it animates by itself at a set speed, giving moving grain with no keyframes.
use_for: Animated film grain over archival recreations or flashbacks
Live grain on still photos in an explainer so they do not feel frozen
Gritty texture under trailer title cards
avoid: High Hue values: rainbow speckle on faces
Using this legacy match name: apply 'ADBE Noise HLS Auto2' instead

params.name: Noise
params.does: Noise style: Uniform, Squared or Grain

params.name: Lightness
params.does: Amount of brightness noise
params.typical: 0.1-0.5 (1 = 100%; 8 wiped the image to static in a test render)

params.name: Saturation
params.does: Amount of saturation noise

params.name: Hue
params.does: Amount of hue noise

params.name: Grain Size
params.does: Grain size, only with Noise = 3

params.name: Noise Animation Speed
params.does: How fast the noise changes (0 freezes it)

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Noise HLS Auto (ADBE Noise HLS Auto2, Noise & Grain); Premiere: Noise (no HLS variant in v26)
cards.scripting: Obsolete: apply 'ADBE Noise HLS Auto2' instead. Hue/Lightness/Saturation harvest here as 0-10 (the current version harvests 0-1000), and a test render confirmed the scale is 1 = 100% (Lightness 8 / Saturation 4 / Hue 1 turned the frame into pure static): divide Noise HLS Auto2 values by 100 (30 there = 0.3 here). Static values only; animation comes from Noise Animation Speed.

verified.note: Now a readable grainy frame with faces, stripes and foreground blocks intact and only faint colour speckle, instead of the full-frame static the old Lightness 8 / Saturation 4 / Hue 1 render produced.

cards.name: Paint
cards.summary: Internal container effect AE adds when you paint on a layer with the Brush, Clone Stamp or Eraser tools; it holds the paint strokes. It is not in the Effects panel and with no strokes it shows nothing.
use_for: Hand-drawn write-on circles or arrows over evidence in an explainer (strokes painted in the UI)
Clone-stamp cleanup of a small blemish or logo on a few frames
Eraser touch-ups on a matte
avoid: Applying it from a script and expecting a visible result: it needs brush strokes
Long frame-by-frame paint jobs: slow to build and fragile to edit

params.name: Paint on Transparent
params.does: Checkbox: show only the strokes on a transparent layer instead of over the layer's pixels

cards.equivalent: No Premiere equivalent (use a shape/mask stroke or a graphic overlay)
cards.scripting: Not superseded but internal: it is not in the Effects panel and is created by the paint tools. A script would have to add stroke groups (likely under 'ADBE Paint Group') with path data, which is not verified (low confidence). For scripted hand-drawn lines prefer a shape layer with Trim Paths or the Stroke / Write-on effects on a mask. 'Paint on Transparent' is a 0/1 checkbox with no harvested range.

verified.note: Hidden internal paint container (status hidden): no gallery frame exists, and with no strokes it would show nothing anyway.

cards.name: Photo Filter
cards.summary: Old version of Photo Filter: mimics a coloured lens filter (warming, cooling, coloured or custom) laid over the image at a set density, optionally keeping brightness unchanged.
use_for: Warm golden tint on rally or ceremony B-roll
Cool blue tint for night, tension or crisis segments
Sepia-style tint for historical flashbacks in a documentary (Filter 13 Sepia here, 15 in ADBE PhotoFilterPS)
avoid: Density above about 60 floods the frame with one colour
Copying Filter indices between this legacy version and ADBE PhotoFilterPS: the lists differ (no LBA / LBB filters here, so Cooling Filter (80) is 3 here and 4 there; Custom is 20 here, 22 there)
Using this legacy match name: apply 'ADBE PhotoFilterPS' instead

params.name: Filter
params.does: Preset lens filter (warming, cooling, colour filters); 1 = Warming Filter (85)

params.name: Color
params.does: Filter colour, used when the custom option is chosen

params.name: Density
params.does: Strength of the tint in percent

params.name: Preserve Luminosity
params.does: Checkbox: keep overall brightness when tinting

cards.equivalent: AE replacement: Photo Filter (ADBE PhotoFilterPS, Color Correction); Premiere: Lumetri Color (Temperature/Tint or Creative tints)
cards.scripting: Obsolete: apply 'ADBE PhotoFilterPS' instead. Filter here is a 1-20 popup (read from After Effects 26.0): 1 Warming Filter (85), 2 Warming Filter (81), 3 Cooling Filter (80), 4 Cooling Filter (82), 5 Red ... 13 Sepia ... 18 Underwater, 19 a separator, 20 Custom; the current version has 22 (with the LBA / LBB filters), so indices do not carry over. Only index 1 has been rendered. Preserve Luminosity is 0/1.

verified.note: Warming Filter (85) at Density 60 gives a clear amber cast over the whole frame (red up, blue down) while brightness stays about the same.
